findings.rationale: Lifecycle sets use the textual correlation_id, while the model transition uses a separately coerced params field. Non-numeric IDs collapse to 0, floats truncate, and an existing params field can disagree with the top-level ID. Consequently pending/completed checks can validate one identity while the monitor mutates another, allowing distinct irreversible-effect keys to target the same modeled payment or aggregate without triggering duplicate detection.

A repeated effect_request with the same effect and correlation ID is silently collapsed by BTreeSet::insert. Duplicate detection occurs only when multiple completions are observed, so concurrent or retried requests can issue an irreversible external effect more than once while a log containing only one completion is reported conformant.
